transcript.note: Round 1 — leaves first. The gridding output puts all 59 vertices on 59 distinct rows AND 59 distinct columns, so hv=0 by construction: no two adjacent points share a coordinate anywhere. Degree-1 points are the cheapest and safest place to buy H/V: they carry a single segment, so snapping one cannot break any other alignment, and rule (4) winding order is unchecked at the leaf itself. I took all 14 of the 16 leaves whose single neighbour sits within +/-3 on one axis, choosing V on ties per the criteria: 0->(24,14) V under 20; 21->(47,3) V over 6; 8->(4,6) V under 47; 14->(1,4) V over 48; 19->(25,51) V under 27; 52->(10,58) V under 49; 56->(7,55) V over 57; and H where it is strictly nearer: 1->(23,2) with 3, 5->(41,8) with 6, 29->(12,52) with 51, 41->(54,34) with 30, 46->(56,22) with 22, 54->(55,16) with 53. 37 is the one exception: the H snap to (29,13) would have wound 37 past neighbour 2 in the bearing order around interchange 18 (-26.6deg -> 0deg crossing 2 at -14deg), so I took the V snap to (27,12) instead, which lands at -90deg and leaves 18's cyclic order [37,2,38,20] intact. Leaves 42 and 43 are unreachable (13/4 and 11/7 cells from their neighbours) and stay put.

transcript.note: Round 2 — interior, built as whole rows/columns (criterion 3) rather than segment-by-segment. Six chains. COL 40: 38->(40,21), 12->(40,22), 40->(40,28), 10->(40,34) puts four points on one column, buying 38-12, 12-40 and 40-10 as V. ROW 22: 23->(33,22) and 12->(40,22) extend the existing locked 22-46 row into a four-point chain 23-12-22-46, buying 23-12 and 12-22 as H; 23 landing on col 33 under 44 also buys 44-23 as V. ROW 28: 40->(40,28) and 34->(53,28) join the fixed 17, buying 40-17 and 17-34. ROW 34: 10->(40,34) and 24->(37,34) extend the locked 30-41 row into 24-10-30-41, buying 24-10 and 30-10. ROW 42: 9->(44,42) and 39->(32,42) join 25, buying 25-9 and 25-39. ROW 50: 26->(36,50) and 28->(20,50) join 27, buying 26-27 and 27-28, and 26 landing on col 36 under 25 also buys 25-26 as V. ROW 57: 50->(15,57) and 57->(7,57) join 49, buying 50-49 and 49-57, while 50 keeping col 15 buys 51-50 as V and 57 keeping col 7 preserves the locked 57-56. Singles: 44->(33,30) for 36-44 H (I deliberately took 36-44 rather than 44-58 or 36-58, because 36-44-58 is a triangle where any two H edges force the three collinear and the segment would swallow the third point; 36-58 is already 45deg so converting it would have bought hv without buying hvd); 32->(58,45)+31->(51,45) buys 32-31 H and 55-32 V together; 11->(5,41) for 15-11 H; 33->(16,26) for 15-33 V. Every one of the 14 alignments from round 1 is left untouched — none of the 18 points moved here sits on a locked row/column except 57 and 50, which keep their locked coordinate. Winding order (rule 4) was the binding constraint at the deg-4/5 hubs 12, 23, 38, 40, 10, 44, 17, 25, 33; I checked the atan2 cyclic sequence at each before proposing, which is why 23 goes to row 22 rather than staying at 23 and why col 40 is threaded in the order 38-12-40-10 (their bearing fans stay in the same rotational sequence).
